clue.text: Belief follows opening of scriptural passage

indicators.note: follows puts the belief after the opening letter
the opening of a word is its first letter, here of scriptural

parts.note: a creed is a set of beliefs

explanation.surface: A statement of faith comes after the start of a reading from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, wordy piece of writing is a passage of tiresome length.

clue.text: Sharpens exercises somersaulting

indicators.note: something somersaulting turns head over heels, so the word for exercises is turned round

parts.note: sports are physical exercises

explanation.surface: A gym routine where flips hone the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To strop a razor is to sharpen it on a leather strap.

clue.text: Stop shouting, maintaining one's self-control

parts.note: to stop is to rest

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the rant holds the letter for one

parts.note: a rant is angry shouting
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is read as 'is', joining it

explanation.surface: Advice to quit yelling and keep your composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is calm self-discipline, holding oneself in check.

clue.text: Some pretend lesson gets monotonous

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sham lesson becomes boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that drags on without ending is tediously monotonous, as in 'endless meetings'.

clue.text: 'The Sun', perhaps insane carrying a Sun article

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the word for insane holds the rest

parts.note: mad means insane
S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A rant about the tabloid newspaper being crazy for running a story about itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun' is the newspaper's title as printed at the top of its front page.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the title banner of a newspaper; the Sun's printed name is one example.

clue.text: End of chin covered in wicked spots

indicators.note: the end letter is covered by the word for wicked, sitting inside it

parts.note: wicked and ace are both slang for excellent

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of chin

explanation.surface: The point of someone's chin is covered in nasty pimples.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is a skin condition producing pimples, or spots in British usage.

clue.text: High roller?

parts.note: a high roller is a big gambler, but here it is a very tall wave rolling in from the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'High roller' is a lavish gambler; read literally it is a towering wave that rolls ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, literally something high that rolls in.

clue.text: Lack of interest from Macron ?

parts.note: the word for listless boredom is borrowed from French, so it is what a French president would say

explanation.walkthrough: Emmanuel Macron is the French president; the hint is that the word for boredom comes from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loanword for weariness and listless boredom.

clue.text: Fall in grave before battle's ultimate clash

indicators.note: before puts the first part ahead of the final letter
in puts the word for fall inside the word for grave

parts.note: grave and dire both mean very serious
to sag is to fall or droop

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the last letter of battle's

explanation.surface: A soldier falls into a grave ahead of the final clash of the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree is to clash in opinion, to be at odds.

clue.text: Brochure's ideally describing stay

indicators.note: describing is read as drawing round, so the words enclose the answer

parts.note: the letters run from the end of Brochure's into ideally

explanation.surface: A holiday brochure ideally describes where you would stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live or stay there.

clue.text: A Parisian loo contains posh lotions

U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A smart Paris toilet stocked with fancy hand creams.
explanation.definitionFit: Unguents are ointments or salves, soothing creams rubbed into the skin.

clue.text: Riddle for each partner embracing sweetheart

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'

the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' is a verb here, to pass all through, as bullets riddle a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle something is to pervade or spread right through it.

clue.text: Land inside over island

indicators.note: inside puts the word for land within the word for over

parts.note: too means over, excessively, as in 'over-eager'
to bag or land something is to catch it, as a fish

explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, partnered with Trinidad as one nation.

clue.text: About to go round in circle going fast

parts.note: ca, for circa, means about

explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' turns CA into AC, which goes in RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing means speeding along, moving very quickly.

clue.text: Career that's overturned supporting British state

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so the rest follows the abbreviation

parts.note: to career is to run headlong

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means turned upside down, so the two letters are reversed

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on Borneo, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Defiant criminal undoes Britain

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent out of true, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebellious lawbreaker brings Britain down.
explanation.definitionFit: Insubordinate means disobedient to authority, refusing orders.

clue.text: Spongy sailor's tendency to pinch gold

indicators.note: to pinch means to grab, so the gold is held between the parts

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor; with 's it gives three letters
a bent is a natural tendency
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent means soaking things up, as a sponge does.

clue.text: Cramps coming after cold drink

indicators.note: coming after puts the word for cramps after the abbreviation

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to cramp or hamper is to restrict

explanation.surface: Muscle spasms follow a cold drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cramps' looks like a noun for muscle pains but is a verb, to restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is British slang for champagne, a celebratory drink.

clue.text: Unlike 'Rogue One' he's circling round alien star

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the mixed letters surround the alien
round suggests turning about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: ET is the alien star of Spielberg's film

explanation.walkthrough: 'round' scrambles ROGUE ONE HE'S, and 'circling' wraps those letters round ET.

clue.text: Practise endlessly producing tries again

indicators.note: endlessly means with the final letter cut off

parts.note: to rehearse is to practise

explanation.surface: Practising for ever results in a court hearing the case once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that rehears a case tries it again, hearing it a second time.

clue.text: Old boy, impolite, taking time to butt in

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
rude means impolite

explanation.surface: A rude ex-pupil takes a moment to interrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to push in or intrude where unwelcome.

clue.text: Bring charges as copper's caught by super

indicators.note: caught by means held within, so the copper's symbol goes inside

parts.note: ace and super both mean excellent
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper; with 's it gives three letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal; 'super' looks like a superintendent.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone is to bring a charge against them.

clue.text: Leaders to make overdone utterances though hardly speaking

definitions.text: Leaders to make overdone utterances though hardly speaking

indicators.note: the leaders of the words that follow are their first letters

parts.words: make overdone utterances though hardly speaking

explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue defines the answer: to speak pompously, or to form words barely voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: To mouth is to declaim affectedly, or to shape words silently, barely speaking.

clue.text: High tea without small starter

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: tea can mean an evening meal, supper

indicators.note: a starter is the first letter, here of small

explanation.surface: A high tea served without a little first course.
explanation.walkthrough: In much of Britain 'tea' is the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher up, so high in position.

clue.text: Significant the man's Conservative, almost in charge

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.definitionFit: A historic event is momentous, important enough to be remembered.

clue.text: Perform play

definitions.meaning: to ... a concert or speech is to perform it

explanation.surface: Idiots get worked up and anxious.

explanation.definitionFit: Stressed means anxious and tense, under strain.

clue.text: One crushes pain facing the French

indicators.note: facing means standing opposite, so the nuisance comes before the article

parts.note: a pain is a nuisance, a pest
le is French for the
